title: Primitive vs Reference Values
concept: Primitives are copied by value, while reference values (objects) are copied by memory address

steps.title: Primitive a = 10
steps.explanation: The number 10 is stored in memory, and a holds that value.
steps.keyInsight: Primitives: number, string, boolean, null, undefined, symbol, bigint

steps.title: b = a (value copy)
steps.explanation:
The value 10 from a is copied and stored in b.
a and b are independent values.

**Analogy**: It's like copying a number written on one piece of paper onto another.
Even if you tear the original paper, the copy is unaffected.
steps.analogy: It's like copying a number written on one piece of paper onto another.

steps.title: b = 20 (independent change)
steps.explanation:
Changing b to 20 doesn't affect a at all.
They occupy separate memory spaces.

steps.title: Printing primitive values
steps.explanation:
a is 10 and b is 20.
Primitives exist independently.

steps.title: Reference obj1 = { value: 10 }
steps.explanation:
Objects are stored in Heap memory.
obj1 holds the address (reference) of that object.

steps.title: obj2 = obj1 (reference copy)
steps.explanation:
The reference (address) of obj1 is copied.
obj1 and obj2 point to the same object!

**Analogy**: It's like two people writing the same home address in their notebooks.
If one person paints the house, the other will also see the painted house when they visit.
steps.keyInsight: Reference values copy the address. There's only one object!
steps.analogy: It's like two people writing the same home address in their notebooks.

steps.title: obj2.value = 20 (modifying the same object)
steps.explanation: When you modify the object through obj2, the change is also visible through obj1!
steps.keyInsight: Same reference = same object = modifying one affects both

steps.title: Printing reference values
steps.explanation:
Both obj1.value and obj2.value are 20.
That's because they both point to the same object.

quiz.explanation:
Arrays are also reference values.
arr2 = arr1 makes them point to the same array.
arr2.push(4) modifies the original array.

misconceptions.wrong: Assigning an object to a variable copies it
misconceptions.correct:
Only the reference (address) is copied.
There's only one object.
misconceptions.why: Objects are stored in the Heap, and variables only hold their addresses.

keyTakeaway: Primitives = copy by value, Reference values = copy by address (same object shared)
